title: Create code-pruning skill
description:
Removal process — the cure that complements YAGNI's prevention.

Sources:
- Five Lines of Code Ch 9 (deleting code), Ch 12 (making bad code look bad)
- Good Code Bad Code Ch 6-7 (antipatterns that become dead weight)
- Research: Meta SCARF (100M+ lines removed), Goldman Sachs code relevance, Kent C. Dodds (commented-out code)
- Research: Language-specific tools (Knip, Vulture, depcheck, PMD)

Content:
- Quick Reference: pruning checklist and detection approach table
- Dead code detection: static analysis, dynamic analysis, combined approach (Meta SCARF)
- Language-specific tool recommendations (date-stamped 2026-02)
- Safe removal process: identify → verify → deprecate → delete → test → audit
- Dependency pruning: unused deps, transitive awareness, false positives
- Commented-out code elimination
- Bloat metrics: dead code %, dependency count, inverse churn, build time trends
- Lava flow antipattern

Deliverable: skills/code-pruning/SKILL.md (300-400 lines)
Cross-references: code-yagni, refactoring-patterns, code-antipatterns
